scope: Independent source review of the five prepared guest SEO detail predicates, their public-page oracle, and rendered SEO UI contract. No browser, heavy test, implementation change, clipboard/Save/provider/database action, or child agent was used.

runtime_verdict.reason: No native-panel run or runtime artifact was examined in this lane. Source validity cannot establish live-page timing, page data, browser navigation, or displayed values.

predicate_review.evidence: The oracle samples anchors from the owned public document and the active panel is scoped through the linked selected SEO tab. Its HTTP(S), host, and count logic closely duplicates src/lib/seo/audit.ts, so it is independent data but not an independent counting oracle.

document.images and absent/blank alt checks sample the real public DOM and align with the UI's conditional Images group. The same product counting rule is reproduced, leaving common-mode false-pass risk.

The panel's word/sentence counts are compared with body.innerText from the owned tab, and the score must be numeric with a recognized band. The sentence split is copied from the production algorithm; the oracle also treats empty innerText as no content although production falls back to body.textContent. The numeric score itself is not independently recomputed, consistent with the bounded prepared claim.

Navigation fields are read from the owned page's PerformanceNavigationTiming, status also has the page.goto response as a second observation, unavailable fields stay null, and UI presence follows SeoDetails' conditional Performance group.

The public DOM supplies alternate/schema values, and actual anchors are checked for destination, target, noopener/noreferrer and trusted pointer activation. Schema collection and schemaDestination reproduce production logic. The anchor-only observation never verifies the visible labels for non-openable plain schema chips. A microdata-only page is also marked unverified because the activation gate requires jsonLdTypeCount > 0.

findings.finding: The expected values are read independently from the public tab, but the oracle repeats the production selectors and algorithms: HTTP(S)/host link classification, img/alt counting, whitespace word count, the exact sentence regex, hreflang selector, JSON-LD traversal, microdata collection, and schema-name resolution. A defect shared by the collector and its copied oracle can therefore pass these predicates. This is source-quality risk, not runtime proof.
findings.repair: Use an independently derived oracle for the claimed values (for example, compare against the public DOM using a distinct implementation/representation and explicit known page invariants), or narrow claims to properties the independent observations can establish. Do not treat matching duplicated algorithms as independent truth.

findings.finding: The schema comparison collects only anchors from the rendered Structured data card. Non-openable schema types intentionally render as plain text chips in SchemaTypeChip, so their visible names are never compared with the public DOM. The hint checks only the total count; a wrong plain-chip type with the same count can pass while the target claims displayed schema values match the page.
findings.repair: Observe every rendered schema chip's visible text, including non-anchor spans, and compare the full displayed type set to the public DOM set; continue checking outbound destinations separately for openable types.

strengths: The new observations are scoped to the selected, active SEO pane and a separately owned public page; they do not consume the audit object as expected data.
The performance check preserves absent timing/status as absent and compares available response status against page.goto's response.
Missing unique hreflang/schema candidates result in an unverified door target rather than a pass, and the path performs no Save, clipboard, provider, authentication, or database action.
limits: No browser or runtime was launched, so all five predicates remain runtime-pending.
The expected metrics are tied to the current public page; no assertions establish that Wikipedia will continue exposing sufficient text, anchors, images, or timing data.
The door target can remain unverified on a page with no usable unique candidates; this is safe accounting but does not demonstrate those doors.

next_action: Resolve the important source-quality findings before the root-owned guarded native run. Keep runtime evidence and source review as separate verdicts.
